newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian family to move to avoid "Cyber-Punk".
newsitem.headline: Canadian family to move to avoid "Cyber-Punk".

text.p: A Canadian family under siege by a prankster dubbed the "Cyber-Punk" has decided to move rather than fight the electronic invasion any longer.

The Tamai family says an unknown stalker who calls himself "Sommy" has been changing television channels, interrupting telephone conversations and cutting power to their home in Emeryville, a small town about 220 miles (354 km) west of Toronto.

Ontario police, as well as telephone and electricity utilities, are continuing to investigate the Tamais' claims but remain perplexed as to how an individual could gain complete control of a private residence.
"I certainly haven't heard anything like this before," said police office Deborah Mineau of the Ontario Provincial Police, who has been investigating the case.
Debbie Tamai said on Thursday her family had had enough.
"We just want to get out of here and start over somewhere else," she said. "We're listing the house now because we don't know how long it will take to sell it."

Ontario police, assisted by hydro and cable experts, began their investigation after the Tamais reported Sommy's antics in January. Since then, Canadian and American media have descended upon the Tamais, but Sommy continues to elude authorities.
Real estate agent Jim Gammon has listed the Tamai's home for C$184,900 ($135,000). He told Reuters no offers have been made, but he has received a flurry of interest.
"I've had calls from around the world, from as far away as Amsterdam and Germany," he said. Sommy has become a bit of a selling point, actually. You never know who might buy the house."
Gammon said he had some advice for the new owners. "I've talked to Sommy myself on the phone, so I'd have a few things to tell the buyers," he said.
